briefs.headline: Exxon slips to $166.87 as oil prices fall and a Venezuela deal stays early
briefs.summary: On November 9, Exxon signed a first, non-binding agreement with Venezuela's state oil company to study oil projects there. Venezuela took over Exxon's projects in 2007, and a $1.6 billion award Exxon won over that is still unpaid. Last quarter Exxon's sales were $113.16 billion, up 32.7% from a year earlier, and its profit per share rose to $4.23 from $1.88. Someone who put $1,000 into Exxon a year ago would have about $1,432 as of November 13.
bull: Profit per share jumped to $4.23 last quarter from $1.88 a year earlier, because oil prices are still far above where they were a year ago.
Exxon's refining business, which turns crude into gasoline and diesel, grew profit 181% to $11.4 billion through September 30, so it earns money even when crude prices fall.
Exxon aims to make a profit even if oil drops to $35 a barrel by 2027, far below today's $92, which gives it room if prices keep sliding.
bear: Brent oil fell to about $92 a barrel on November 16 after trading as high as $120 during the Iran conflict, and lower oil means less profit per barrel.
The Venezuela deal does not commit Exxon to any project, and Exxon still needs a real contract and stable rules before it would invest.
The stock lost 4.7% in a month, more than the S&P 500's 3.1%, and sits about 11% below its 52-week high of $188.50.

briefs.headline: J&J buys eye-drug maker Ollin for up to $3.3 billion after a record close
briefs.summary: On November 16, J&J agreed to buy Ollin Biosciences for $2.2 billion in cash plus up to about $1.13 billion more if goals are met, with the deal expected to close before the end of 2026. Ollin's main drug, OLN324, is in its final stage of testing for wet AMD and diabetic eye swelling, two causes of vision loss. Blackstone will pay J&J $750 million over several years to fund that testing, in return for a small cut of future sales. Earlier, the FDA approved Rybrevant Faspro for head and neck cancer on November 5, and Caplyta passed a second final-stage bipolar test on November 10.
bull: Tremfya, an immune drug, grew sales 68% to $2.40 billion last quarter, and the CEO says it can become a $10 billion-a-year drug.
Blackstone pays $750 million toward Ollin's final testing, so J&J takes on less of the cost and risk of the new eye drug.
A new psoriatic arthritis pill, Icotyde, helped 58% of patients in a final-stage test on November 7, adding another possible big seller.
bear: At 42.8 times its past-year profit, J&J costs about twice as much as the average S&P 500 stock, so bad news could hit the price hard.
Products with $4 to $4.5 billion in yearly sales lose patent protection in 2027, which lets cheaper copies take sales away.
The stock trades above analysts' average price goal of about $279, and two recent deals cut 2026 profit per share by $0.64.

briefs.name: Micron Technology
briefs.whyMoved: Micron fell about 6% on November 16, trading near $730 at midday after closing at $778.31 on November 13, its third drop in a row. Reports said the US government is adding a new rule that limits AI chips and computing going to China and makes buyers in places like Singapore, Malaysia and Brazil get export licenses, which could mean fewer memory chips sold. Investors also worry that Nvidia, the biggest buyer of Micron's AI memory, could slow orders after CEO Jensen Huang resigned. Almost all of Micron's huge profit now comes from selling memory for AI data centers, so any sign that AI chip buying slows hits the stock hard.

watch.what: Nvidia reports results after the close. Strong AI chip sales and a confident new leader would ease fears about memory orders; a weak outlook could push Micron lower.
Micron's expected quarterly report (estimated date). Good: sales near or above $61.5 billion. Bad: a lower forecast or falling memory prices.

market.why: On Friday, November 13, the Nasdaq and S&P 500 fell as chip stocks kept sliding, with AMD down about 9% and Nvidia down about 2% a day after its CEO Jensen Huang quit. The 10-year Treasury rate, what the government pays to borrow, hit about 5.17%, which weighs on smaller companies in the Russell 2000. The Dow ended slightly higher since it holds fewer chip stocks, and the S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow still rose about 2% for the week.
